hypotheses.justification: A proof needs only finite coproducts and normal epimorphisms. First, KernelFork.IsLimit.lift' applied to l shows that a ≫ f = 0 implies a = 0. Given u,v : T ⟶ X with u ≫ f = v ≫ f, set p = coprod.desc (𝟙 X) u and q = coprod.desc (𝟙 X) v. Then p ≫ f = q ≫ f. The split epimorphism p is normal by normalEpiOfEpi; write its cokernel witness as w with w ≫ p = 0. Zero cancellation gives w ≫ q = 0, so CokernelCofork.IsColimit.desc' gives h with p ≫ h = q. Precomposing with coprod.inl shows h = 𝟙 X, and precomposing with coprod.inr then gives u = v. No global cokernel existence is used. This argument also covers zero and trivial objects without additional assumptions.
